key_insight: The paper formalizes how to compare the safety of candidate LLMs when no labeled benchmark exists by treating scenario-based audits as valid evidence only under a specified audit contract (scenario pack, rubric, auditor, judge, sampling, rerun budget). It replaces reliance on ground-truth labels with controlled, contract-bound comparative scoring and uncertainty quantification.
problem_solved: How to reliably compare and validate the safety of language models for deployment when there is no existing labeled benchmark for the target language, sector, or regulatory context.
method: Formalize "benchmarkless comparative safety scoring" and define an explicit audit contract: scenario pack, rubric, auditor, judge, sampling configuration, and rerun budget.
Run scenario-based audits (curated or generated scenarios) under the contract to elicit model behavior and produce comparative scores instead of relying on unavailable labels.
Use controlled sampling and rerun-budget protocols to quantify uncertainty and make comparative scores interpretable and reproducible only within the specified contract.
impact: Enables practitioners and regulators to produce transparent, repeatable safety comparisons for LLM deployment even when no labeled benchmark exists, helping informed decisions and compliance with contextual safety requirements.
visual_elements: Audit contract diagram showing components: scenario pack, rubric, auditor, judge, sampling config, rerun budget
Flowchart of the audit process: create scenarios → run models → score under rubric → aggregate comparative scores with uncertainty
Comparison chart (e.g., side-by-side bars or violin plots) showing model safety scores with uncertainty bands and annotation that scores are valid only under the contract
Checklist/icon set emphasizing reproducibility elements (fixed scenarios, rubric, auditor, sampling, rerun budget)
paper_title: When No Benchmark Exists: Validating Comparative LLM Safety Scoring Without Ground-Truth Labels
paper_authors: Sushant Gautam, Finn Schwall, Annika Willoch Olstad, Fernando Vallecillos Ruiz, Birk Torpmann-Hagen
